entry.title: vm2: NodeVM nesting guard accepts array-shaped require and permits host RCE (CVE-2026-92935)
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce · CVE-2026-92935

vm2 NodeVM is vulnerable to a nesting guard bypass (CVE-2026-92935) where passing an array for the require parameter bypasses type checking, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code on the host system with critical severity. The vulnerability affects versions of vm2 where `typeof requireOpts === 'object'` accepts arrays, which then destructure to undefined and permit nesting execution. This is exploitable in the wild when downstream NodeVM instances are configured with `nesting: true` and untrusted code execution. Patch immediately by updating vm2 to a patched version and add strict type validation for require configuration parameters.

entry.title: vm2: NodeVM node:-prefixed negative builtin deny bypass exposes child_process (CVE-2026-92957)
entry.content:

The npm vm2 package (NodeVM) contains a critical sandbox escape vulnerability (CVE-2026-92957) where negative builtin denials fail to block `node:`-prefixed module specifiers, allowing sandboxed code to require child_process and execute arbitrary processes despite explicit deny policies. This affects configurations using wildcard builtin policies with negative entries like `['*', '-node:child_process']`. The vulnerability is critical severity and likely exploitable in active deployments using vm2 for code sandboxing. Users should immediately update to a patched version once released or implement external process isolation controls as a mitigation.

entry.title: PyJWT: Asymmetric-PEM detection bypass: whitespace/line-ending-mutated public keys skip the HS/asymmetric confusion guard (CVE-2026-102268)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-102268

PyJWT versions prior to patching are vulnerable to asymmetric-HMAC confusion attacks when decoding JWT tokens if the allow-list contains both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms (CVE-2026-102268, critical severity). The vulnerability exploits a bypass in PyJWT's PEM format detection where whitespace or line-ending mutations in public keys cause the `is_pem_format` regex to fail, allowing an attacker with a valid HMAC secret to forge tokens that pass asymmetric signature verification. This impacts deployments mixing algorithm types in the decode allow-list and passing PEM keys as raw bytes/text. Immediately update PyJWT to the patched version and audit configurations to follow RFC 8725 best practices by using single asymmetric algorithms in decode allow-lists rather than mixing HS/asymmetric options.

The VM uses a lightweight bytecode interpreter with 14 opcode handlers performing simple operations (XOR, addition, rotation, substitution), while the custom stream ciphers vary their constants and transformations across builds. This represents an ongoing threat with active development; no severity rating or exploitation metrics are provided in the source material. Organizations should employ behavioral detection, network monitoring for command-and-control communication, and endpoint detection systems capable of identifying stealer activity patterns rather than relying solely on signature-based detection of these increasingly polymorphic obfuscation techniques.

vulnerability · privilege-escalation · CVE-2026-87886

Acronis Backup plugins for cPanel & WHM and Plesk contain an incorrect default permissions vulnerability (CVE-2026-87886) enabling privilege escalation attacks. entry.title: NetNTLMv1 Is Dead. Long Live NetNTLMv1.
entry.content:
red-team · credential-cracking

NetNTLMv1 authentication protocol is now trivially crackable using publicly released rainbow tables and GPU acceleration tools (WebGPU browser client and ntlmrain CLI). Attackers can recover NT hashes from captured NetNTLMv1 responses with fixed challenge 1122334455667788 using commodity hardware (4TB disk, standard GPU), making this authentication method cryptographically broken. This technique is actively exploited in the wild as practical attack tools are publicly available. Organizations must disable NetNTLMv1 immediately and enforce NTLMv2 or Kerberos; any systems still relying on NetNTLMv1 for authentication should be considered compromised if network traffic was captured.

Read more · Source: outflank

entry.title: The Shared Clipboard Inside the Sandbox: Cross-Account Data Leakage in ChatGPT
entry.content:
vulnerability · data-leakage

ChatGPT's code execution sandbox contains a cross-account data leakage vulnerability where the shared clipboard is accessible across different user sessions, allowing attackers to exfiltrate sensitive information pasted by other users. An attacker can inject malicious code into their ChatGPT conversation that reads clipboard contents, potentially capturing passwords, API keys, and private data from concurrent users. This vulnerability has moderate severity as it requires active exploitation during simultaneous sessions but affects a widely-used platform with millions of users; Check Point Research has not indicated active exploitation in the wild. Users should avoid pasting sensitive credentials directly into ChatGPT, and OpenAI should implement per-user clipboard isolation in the sandbox environment.

Read more · Source: checkpoint-research

entry.title: Netty: SNI Routing Bypass via Fragmented TLS ClientHello Causing Fallback to Default SslContext (CVE-2026-75595)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-75595

Netty handler (io.netty:netty-handler) contains a critical vulnerability in SslClientHelloHandler#decode where fragmented TLS ClientHello messages bypass SNI-based routing by causing fallback to the default SslContext. An attacker can craft a malicious ClientHello with the handshake header spanning multiple records to trigger this behavior, bypassing mTLS authentication gates that rely solely on per-SNI selection. This vulnerability is likely exploitable in the wild given its trivial exploitation method. Immediately patch to the latest Netty version and validate that your mTLS implementations do not depend exclusively on SNI-based SslContext selection.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.title: August updates trigger 0xc0000409 errors on Windows Server 2016
entry.content:
vulnerability · denial-of-service

Windows Server 2016 systems running August 2026 security updates may experience 0xc0000409 errors when the Compatibility Appraiser diagnostic service is active. This is a reliability issue rather than a security vulnerability, causing system instability and potential crashes. Microsoft has acknowledged the problem but no exploit in the wild has been reported. Affected organizations should either disable the Compatibility Appraiser service if not required, defer the August update pending a fix, or apply workarounds documented in Microsoft's advisory.

entry.title: ChatGPT Flaw Let a Planted Prompt Send a Victim's Gmail Data to Another Account
entry.content:
vulnerability · prompt-injection · CVE-2026-61732

ChatGPT's plugin system was vulnerable to prompt injection attacks where a malicious instruction embedded in user-supplied content could execute hidden operations while the assistant continued normal functionality. In the proof-of-concept, attackers could exfiltrate Gmail data connected to a victim's account and relay it to attacker-controlled accounts via covert channels. This was a high-severity vulnerability affecting users with Gmail integration enabled, though no evidence of active exploitation in the wild was reported. OpenAI patched the underlying plugin isolation issues; users should disable unnecessary third-party integrations and review plugin permissions settings.

entry.title: FreeIPA Flaw Chain Lets Anonymous Clients Create Reusable Administrator Credentials
entry.content:
vulnerability · privilege-escalation

FreeIPA identity management system is vulnerable to a privilege escalation chain allowing unauthenticated clients to create arbitrary Kerberos identities with administrator privileges through flaws in both FreeIPA and the underlying 389 Directory Server. The vulnerability requires no prior authentication and leverages LDAP access to inject malicious directory entries that grant administrative group membership. This is a critical severity issue with potential for exploitation in environments where FreeIPA is exposed to untrusted networks. Immediate patching of both FreeIPA and 389 Directory Server is required; isolate FreeIPA administration interfaces and restrict LDAP access to trusted networks pending updates.
